historical_references.reference: The name Damion is derived from the Greek name Damianos, which means 'tamer of wild animals'. It was a common name among early Christians, particularly among the saints. One notable Saint Damian was Damian and Cosmas, two brothers who were physicians and Christian martyrs. They were born in Syria and were buried in Rome. Their feast day is celebrated on September 1st.

Another Saint Damian is Damian of Moloka'i, also known as Damian of Hawaii. He was a Catholic priest who lived in Hawaii in the late 19th century. He is best known for his work in caring for the lepers of Moloka'i. He died of leprosy on April 15, 1889, and is now considered a patron saint of lepers.
historical_references.context: Catholic priest and patron saint of lepers
